note: Two sites about 150 m apart on Red Ridge Road, roughly 1.4 to 1.5 miles from McConnell Road and 2.2 miles from Windfall Road: 026 Red Ridge Well Pad on a grass clearing, and 033 Twin Sisters on a small dirt pad that the agency says is shared with access and parking for the Twin Sisters Trail, where hikers may be encountered. The agency cautions that it is reached by dirt or gravel forest roads that may not suit low-clearance vehicles or large RVs. Stone fire rings; no table, toilet or water. Pack out trash. --Claude
summary: Both site pages re-read: 026 and 033 still listed, Drive-In, RV/Tent/Trailer categories, max vehicle and equipment length 40 ft, back-in dirt driveways 40 ft, grades Slight; count 2 and 40 ft confirmed, pull_through false and a sites note added. Year-round confirmed; both sell in all five windows (some November nights Reserved). Fees confirmed, $6.50 reservation fee added; hookups and facilities none. Imagery (Esri leaf-on only): 026's point in a grass clearing about 50 x 35 m, open to the sky; 033's point about 10 m east of a dirt patch roughly 15 m across with a vehicle on it; the road between them is under canopy. Pin is on 026. NHD: nothing within 200 m of either; not waterfront.
flags: Are the two together: yes. 026 (41.57378,-77.84891) and 033 (41.57270,-77.84773) are about 155 m apart on the same road by the pages' own mileages (1.4 and 1.5 miles from McConnell Road). One entry; the stored pin equals 026's point.

What kind of place 033 is: the page says 'Campsite is shared with access/parking to Twin Sisters Trail. Hikers may be encountered.' That is a hiking-trail parking spot, not an ATV or horse-trailer lot (ruling 1 concerns ATV parking; the page names no ATV use). Kept, with the wording in the note. Imagery shows a dirt patch roughly 15 m across, which is small for a shared trailhead and a 40-ft site; observation only.
Ground at 026: the name says well pad; no page read describes it, and imagery shows a grass clearing about 50 x 35 m with no structures visible.

Agency access statements (ruling 11: nothing measured, no road surface, gate or bridge research): 'Caution: This campsite is accessed by state forest dirt or gravel roads and may not be suitable for some low-clearance vehicles or large RVs.' (both pages) 'Site Grade: Slight', 'Driveway Grade: Slight', 'Driveway Surface: Dirt', 'Site Height/Overhead Clearance: 20'. No Severe grade, no 4WD or wet-weather statement, no closure. Kept. The page also carries the district-wide 'Road and Travel Alert' and '4WD vehicles may be recommended for some sites year-round, check notes' boilerplate (this site's notes say nothing about 4WD).

ATV check (ruling 1): the site page(s) say nothing about ATVs and do not call the ground a parking area. The DCNR Susquehannock ATV Trail brochure names five trailheads (District Office, Sunken Branch, Route 44, Rock Run, Lyman); none is this site. The camp at the Rock Run trailhead is a separate site, '029 Rock Run ATV' in the DCNR GIS layer, not part of this entry. Kept.
NAME: the stored name carries the site's own name and road as the booking system gives them ('Site, Loop: 026 Red Ridge Well Pad / 033 Twin Sisters, Red Ridge Rd'); nothing to change.
Equestrian check: the Susquehannock camping page names the Dyer and Horsey Hilton equestrian areas; this entry is neither and its page(s) list no horse category.

Susquehannock advisories page (read 2026-11-10): district office closure Oct 17-18, 2026; Rausch Road reopened July 31, 2025; 'Stay Alert for ATVs on Roads' (the Northcentral Regional ATV Trail uses some PennDOT, township and forest roads); a dust advisory. No road closure, gate, bridge limit or timber-sale notice, and nothing on this entry's road. The camping page publishes no seasonal closure or site rotation.
